trial_court: JMFC, Gwalior in Criminal Case No.1515/2007

parties.respondent_defendant: Jasvant Singh & Anr. (husband and another person)

facts_of_case: The applicant was married to respondent no.1 in 1982 and had six children. Respondent no.1 obtained a decree of divorce on false grounds and the applicant filed an appeal against it. Despite the appeal being filed, respondent no.1 performed second marriage with respondent no.2.

legal_principles.principle: A divorced person shall be entitled to marry again after the time of appealing has expired, without an appeal having been presented or an appeal having been dismissed.
legal_principles.held: From the plain reading of this provision, it is clear that a divorced person shall be entitled to marry again after the time of appealing has expired, without an appeal having been presented or an appeal having been dismissed.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking to establish that the other party has committed an offence under Section 494 of IPC.
legal_principles.held: It is also not in dispute that the appeal filed by the applicant against the decree of divorce has also been dismissed. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

outcome.final_order: The respondents were acquitted of the charge under Section 494,34 of IPC.
